michael-r-adams.text: Voted with the 4-1 majority (Mar. 2025; only Michael Rives opposed) for a $251,800 contract with TeamCivX to help prepare a possible November 2026 AVC bond measure.

source.title: AV Press: AVC trustees mull 2026 bond (Mar. 14, 2025)

michael-r-adams.text: Voted with the 4-1 majority (Apr. 2025; only Rives dissented) to abolish nine vacant classified positions after the classified union asked that the move be bargained first.

source.title: AV Press: College board eliminates 3 staff positions (Apr. 17, 2025)

michael-r-adams.text: Voted (May 2025, 4-0) to raise the cap on Atkinson, Andelson, Loya, Ruud & Romo legal fees by $175,000 to $375,000, over objections from both employee unions.

source.title: AV Press: Union leaders protest AVC spending hike (May 17, 2025)

michael-r-adams.text: Voted with the 4-1 majority (Nov. 2025; only Michelle Harvey dissented) for a rolling three-year contract for Superintendent/President Jennifer Zellet, whose salary is about $311,692.

source.title: AV Press: AV College head gets three-year employment deal (Nov. 22, 2025)

michael-r-adams.text: (2024) As board president, responding to employee complaints about dismissals: "We discuss every personnel issue in depth... We take no personnel decision easily... We do nothing without a lot of heart for our employees at the college."

source.title: AV Press: AVC workers' treatment draws ire (Dec. 24, 2024)

michael-r-adams.text: As board president, announced the board's 4-1 vote (Aug. 2025) to settle the faculty union's labor-board case over eliminating the winter intersession, compensating affected faculty.

source.title: AV Press: AVC board OKs new pact with teachers (Aug. 14, 2025)

nashon-t-mitchell.text: Endorsed by the LA County Democratic Party.

source.title: LA County Democratic Party: 2026 Endorsed Candidates

notes: Adams: board votes and statements as reported by the Antelope Valley Press. Where AV Press gives a 4-1 tally naming the lone dissenter, or a 4-0 tally naming the one absentee, his yes vote is inferred. Mitchell: only the LACDP endorsement; no campaign site, survey or policy statements found (AV Press mentions him only as founder of a community nonprofit). Searches used: 9
